historical_v1_note: v1 (schema c72-formby-eval-v1, final/formby/formby_results.json) is unchanged. Its NB and GMM used early/late blocks (repetitions 1-8 train, 9-16 test); its FF-ANN used Formby's random 75/25 window split, so FF-ANN test windows came from blocks that also supplied training windows. v1 predictions used scikit-learn predict() (sorted class order for exact ties) and are not rewritten here.

protocol.ba: mean over test blocks of per-block balanced accuracy
protocol.converged_fraction: converged fits / fits behind the cell: NB 1, GMM 1, FF-ANN inner-CV fits + 1 final
protocol.convergence: NB closed form (converged); GMM converged_ and no ConvergenceWarning; FF-ANN n_iter_ < max_iter and no ConvergenceWarning, captured per fit

ff_ann.selection: GroupKFold(min(5, training blocks)) over training blocks; highest mean validation BA; a tie keeps the smaller size

protocol.gmm: GaussianMixture(3, full, reg_covar=1e-6, n_init=10, random_state=seed); Hungarian map from training labels; score = posterior probability of the mapped component

high.ff_ann: 1.05 x the largest value in the training windows; refitted inside every inner fold
high.gmm: not used: raw window [mean, variance], no standardisation
high.nb: 1.05 x the largest training-row value of the training arm (v1 rule)

protocol.histogram: Formby Eq. 1: 199 equal bins on [0, H) plus one overflow bin for x >= H

observers.pre_deployment: trained on off at the same D, tested on each arm (off included)
observers.retrained: trained on the arm's own training blocks

protocol.paired_delta: off minus arm per matched test repetition, bootstrapped over repetitions; positive means the arm lowered BA
protocol.split: grouped chronological, per D: repetitions 1-8 train, 9-16 test; shared by NB, GMM and FF-ANN
protocol.tie_rule: classes whose score is within 1e-09 of the row maximum are tied; the tie goes to the first of them in the fixed order READ, SELECT, OPERATE; a window whose top-two margin is below 1e-09 counts as a near-tie
protocol.windows: same-operation, non-overlapping, inside one block and arm, from the first row (v1 rule)

request_to_first_response_byte: not a separate feature: resp_segments == 1 for 49408 of 49408 rows, so every response arrived in one captured TCP segment and request->first response byte equals rt_ms (request->complete response)
task: operation classification (READ/SELECT/OPERATE), one SEL-751; not device identification
